title: Credit and Collections Policy for Northgate Business Invoice Accounts (Net Terms): Late Charges, Courtesy Waivers, Credit Holds and Collections Referral
content:
On each statement day, Northgate Business Invoice Accounts (Net Terms) charge the tier's late charge percent on the principal of invoices unpaid more than the tier's grace days after their due date, as simple interest with no charge on earlier late charges, and at least the tier's smallest late charge when any is due; amounts under invoice dispute are excluded. A tier whose late charge percent is 0.0 never charges one.

## 1. Late charges

1.1 The late charge is assessed on the statement day and is computed on the past-due invoice principal at the statement date, as simple interest; earlier late charges bear no charge.

1.2 An invoice's principal enters the charge when, on the statement date, the invoice is unpaid more than the tier's grace days after its due date. An invoice exactly the grace days after its due date does not yet enter it.

1.3 Amounts under invoice dispute are excluded from the principal charged, where the tier excludes disputed amounts from late charges.

1.4 The charge is the late charge percent of that principal, rounded half up to the cent, and is not less than the tier's smallest late charge in any month in which a charge is due.

1.5 A late charge adds to the amount the business owes on its invoice account.

**Worked example (hypothetical account; 1.5 percent, $5.00 smallest charge, 5 grace days; statement on 1 October).**

| Invoice | Unpaid principal | Due date | Days after due on 1 October | Disputed | Principal entering the charge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | $820.00 | 20 September | 11 | None | $820.00 |
| B | $410.00 | 26 September | 5 | None | $0.00 |
| C | $380.00 | 25 September | 6 | $80.00 | $300.00 |

The principal charged is $820.00 and $300.00, a total of $1120.00; 1.5 percent of it is $16.80, above the $5.00 smallest charge, so the late charge is $16.80. Had only $250.00 entered the charge, 1.5 percent would be $3.75 and the charge would be the $5.00 smallest charge.

## 2. Credit hold and release

2.1 New invoiced orders are put on credit hold when the account's days past due reach the tier's credit hold figure, or when the balance exceeds the credit line by more than the tier's over-line tolerance percent. The hold records its reason as past due or over line.

2.2 Days past due are the calendar days from the due date of the oldest unpaid, undisputed invoice to the date being evaluated; they are 0 when no undisputed invoice is unpaid after its due date.

2.3 The hold is released once both conditions clear.

| Hypothetical case | Judgement |
|---|---|
| Hold figure 30 days; oldest unpaid, undisputed invoice due 1 August; evaluated 30 August (29 days) | Past-due condition not reached |
| Same; evaluated 31 August (30 days) | Past-due condition reached: credit hold |
| Line $20000, tolerance 5.0 percent; balance $21000.00 | Exceeds the line by exactly 5.0 percent, not more: no over-line hold |
| Same; balance $21000.01 | Exceeds by more than 5.0 percent: credit hold |

## 3. Collections referral

An account on hold that reaches the tier's collections days past due is closed and referred to collections.

## 4. Waivers

4.1 A late charge may be waived as a courtesy only while the number of courtesy waivers on the account in the rolling 12 calendar months ending on the waiver date, that date included, is below the tier's courtesy-waiver allowance.

4.2 A charge made in error is always reversed as a billing error.

4.3 A waiver reduces the amount the business owes on its invoice account by the amount waived.

*Hypothetical:* on a tier allowing 1 courtesy waiver in 12 months, an account with no courtesy waiver in the 12 months ending on the waiver date is below the allowance; an account with 1 such waiver is not, and a further late charge cannot be waived as a courtesy. A charge made in error is reversed as a billing error in either case.
